passages.text: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Jew.
Paul stood before the people.
Paul spoke to the people.
Paul said, “Brothers and fathers, listen to me now.”
Paul said, “I will give my defense before you.”
passages.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας

passages.text: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more silent. Then Paul declared, “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I am just as zealous for God as any of you here today.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before the crowd.
Paul spoke to the people in Hebrew.
The people heard Paul speak in Hebrew.
The people became even more silent.
Paul said, “I am a Jew.
I was born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia.
I grew up in this city.
I learned at the feet of Gamaliel.
Gamaliel taught me carefully according to the law of our ancestors.
I am zealous for God.
I am as zealous as all of you are today.”
passages.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν Καὶ φησίν Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ Θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον

passages.text: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison, as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the crowd.
Paul was a Jew.
Paul persecuted followers of Jesus.
Paul persecuted them even to death.
Paul arrested men who followed Jesus.
Paul arrested women who followed Jesus.
Paul put these people in prison.
The high priest saw what Paul did.
The whole Council saw what Paul did.
The high priest and the Council can testify about Paul.
Paul received letters from the high priest and the Council.
These letters were for the brothers in Damascus.
Paul traveled to Damascus.
Paul planned to arrest followers of Jesus in Damascus.
Paul planned to bring them to Jerusalem.
Paul wanted them to be punished.
passages.original: ὃς ταύτην τὴν Ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον παρ’ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν

passages.text: About noon as I was approaching Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.
passages.sermon:
Paul was traveling to Damascus.
It was about noon.
Paul came near the city.
Suddenly, a bright light flashed.
The light came from heaven.
The light shone all around Paul.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ

passages.text: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’
passages.sermon:
Paul was traveling to Damascus to arrest Christians.
\r\nHe was a persecutor of Christians.
\r\nHe fell to the ground.
\r\nHe heard a voice.
\r\nThe voice spoke to him.
\r\nThe voice said, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”
passages.original: ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι Σαοὺλ Σαούλ τί με διώκεις

passages.text: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke to the voice.
Saul asked, "Who are You, Lord?"
The voice answered Saul.
The voice said, "I am Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus said, "You are persecuting Me."
passages.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην Τίς εἶ Κύριε Εἶπέν τε πρὸς ἐμέ Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις

passages.text: My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.
passages.sermon: My companions were with me.\r\nThey saw the light.\r\nThey did not understand the voice of the One who spoke to me.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ἐθεάσαντο τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι

passages.text: Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ ‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’
passages.sermon:
I spoke to the Lord.
I asked, "What should I do, Lord?"
The Lord answered me.
He said, "Get up."
He said, "Go into Damascus."
He said, "There, someone will tell you everything you must do."
God has chosen these things for you to do.
passages.original: Εἶπον δέ Τί ποιήσω Κύριε Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εἶπεν πρός με Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι

passages.text: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.
passages.sermon:
The light was very bright.
The light was glorious.
The light blinded me.
I could not see.
My companions were with me.
They took me by the hand.
They led me into Damascus.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν

passages.text: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there, came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.
passages.sermon:
Ananias was a man.
He was devout.
He followed the law.
All the Jews living in Damascus respected him.
Ananias came to me.
He stood beside me.
He spoke to me.
He said, “Brother Saul, receive your sight.”
At that moment, I could see him.
passages.original: Ἁνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ ἀνάβλεψον κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear His voice.
passages.sermon:
Ananias spoke to me.
Ananias was a devout man.
He followed the law.
All the Jews in Damascus respected him.
Ananias said, “The God of our fathers has chosen you.”
God has appointed you to know His will.
God has appointed you to see the Righteous One.
God has appointed you to hear the voice from His mouth.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν Δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ

passages.text: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.
passages.sermon:
God chose you, Saul.
You have seen and heard important things from God.
You will tell everyone about these things.
You will be a witness for God to all people.
You will speak about what you have seen.
You will speak about what you have heard.
passages.original: ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας

passages.text: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name.’
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to a man who had seen Jesus and heard His voice.
Paul said, “Do not wait any longer.
Stand up now.
Be baptized.
Let baptism wash away your sins.
Call on the name of Jesus.”
passages.original: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’
passages.sermon:
I returned to Jerusalem.
I prayed at the temple.
While I prayed, I fell into a trance.
I saw the Lord.
The Lord spoke to me.
He said, “Hurry!
Leave Jerusalem quickly.
The people here will not accept your testimony about Me.”
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the Lord.
Paul said, “Lord, the people know what I did.
They know I went from synagogue to synagogue.
They know I imprisoned those who believed in You.
They know I beat those who believed in You.”
passages.original: Κἀγὼ εἶπον Κύριε αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ

passages.text: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’
passages.sermon:
Stephen was your witness.
People killed Stephen.
They shed his blood.
I stood there.
I agreed with what they did.
I watched over the clothes of those who killed him.
passages.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν

passages.text: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to me.
He gave me a command.
He said, "Go."
He said, "I will send you."
He said, "I will send you far away."
He said, "I will send you to the Gentiles."
The Gentiles are people who are not Jews.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν πρός με Πορεύου ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε

passages.text: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement. Then they lifted up their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the crowd.
The crowd listened to Paul.
They listened until Paul made this statement.
Then the crowd raised their voices.
They shouted loudly.
They said, “Remove this man from the earth!”
They said, “He is not fit to live!”
passages.original: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν

passages.text: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air, the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him.
passages.sermon:
The crowd shouted loudly.
They threw off their cloaks.
They tossed dust into the air.
The Roman commander saw this chaos.
He ordered his soldiers to bring Paul into the barracks.
He told them to flog Paul.
He wanted Paul to be questioned under flogging.
He wanted to find out why the crowd was shouting against Paul.
passages.original: Κραυγαζόντων τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα ἐκέλευσεν ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ

passages.text: But as they stretched him out to strap him down, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Roman citizen.
\r\nThe soldiers stretched Paul out.
\r\nThey prepared to tie him down with straps.
\r\nA centurion stood nearby.
\r\nPaul spoke to the centurion.
\r\nPaul asked a question.
\r\nHe said, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen who has not been condemned?”
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν

passages.text: On hearing this, the centurion went and reported it to the commander. “What are you going to do?” he said. “This man is a Roman citizen.”
passages.sermon:
A centurion heard Paul speak.
Paul said he was a Roman citizen.
The centurion went to the commander.
He reported the situation to the commander.
He said, “What are you going to do?”
He said, “This man is a Roman citizen.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν λέγων Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν

passages.text: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” he answered.
passages.sermon:
The commander went to Paul.
The commander spoke to Paul.
The commander asked Paul a question.
The commander said, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?”
Paul answered the commander.
Paul said, “Yes.”
passages.original: Προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Λέγε μοι σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Ναί

passages.text: “I paid a high price for my citizenship,” said the commander. “But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.
passages.sermon:
The commander spoke to Paul.
The commander said, “I paid a large sum for my Roman citizenship.”
Paul answered the commander.
Paul said, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην ὁ Δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι

passages.text: Then those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Roman citizen.
Some men were about to interrogate Paul.
These men stepped back from Paul immediately.
The commander had put Paul in chains.
The commander realized Paul was a Roman citizen.
The commander became afraid.
passages.original: Εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν ἦν δεδεκώς

passages.text: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.
passages.sermon:
The commander was in charge.
He wanted to know why the Jews accused Paul.
The next day, the commander released Paul from his chains.
He ordered the chief priests to gather.
He also ordered the whole Sanhedrin to assemble.
The commander brought Paul to them.
He made Paul stand before the group.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν αὐτόν καὶ ἐκέλευσεν συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ πᾶν τὸ συνέδριον καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς
